Model 2: the map $(t,x,v)\mapsto m\mathbf g-c\,v$ is a constant plus a scalar multiple of the linear map $v\mapsto v$, hence continuous by [L3]; and for states $z=(x,v)$, $z'=(x',v')$, $\lVert F(t,z)-F(t,z')\rVert_{2}=\lVert c(v'-v)\rVert_{2}=c\,\lVert v-v'\rVert_{2}\le c\,\lVert z-z'\rVert_{2}$ by [L2], so $L=c$ is a state-Lipschitz constant on every cylinder and does not depend on time; in particular model 2 satisfies [L1].

Then $$\Bigl\lVert\frac{x}{\lvert x\rvert^{3}}-\frac{y}{\lvert y\rvert^{3}}\Bigr\rVert_{2}\le\frac{\lVert x-y\rVert_{2}}{\lvert x\rvert^{3}}+\lvert y\rvert\,\bigl|\lvert x\rvert^{-3}-\lvert y\rvert^{-3}\bigr|\le\frac{\lVert x-y\rVert_{2}}{r^{3}}+R\cdot\frac{3R^{2}}{r^{6}}\lVert x-y\rVert_{2},$$ where the first inequality inserts $y/\lvert x\rvert^{3}$ and uses the triangle inequality, and the second uses $\bigl|\lvert x\rvert^{-3}-\lvert y\rvert^{-3}\bigr|\le 3R^{2}r^{-6}\bigl|\lvert x\rvert-\lvert y\rvert\bigr|\le 3R^{2}r^{-6}\lVert x-y\rVert_{2}$, the factorization $\lvert v^{3}-u^{3}\rvert=\lvert v-u\rvert\,(v^{2}+vu+u^{2})$ applied to $u=\lvert x\rvert$, $v=\lvert y\rvert$ and the reverse triangle inequality of [L2]; multiplying by $k$ gives the constant $L=k(r^{-3}+3R^{3}r^{-6})$ for $F=-kx/\lvert x\rvert^{3}$ on the annulus (the state variable enters only through $x$).

Model 3, no extension to the excluded point: for $x\ne0$ one has $\lVert F(x)\rVert_{2}=k\lvert x\rvert^{-2}$, so for every bound $M>0$ there is $\delta=\sqrt{k/M}>0$ with $\lVert F(x)\rVert_{2}>M$ whenever $0<\lvert x\rvert<\delta$; hence no continuous extension of $F$ to $x=0$ exists ([[def-continuity-real]]: a continuous extension would carry a sequence $x_{n}\to0$ to a convergent image sequence, but the values are unbounded).
